additional_logical_suppliers.exact_interface_excerpt: A homotopy type $X$ is **locally finite** if every homotopy group $\pi_i(X,x)$ is finite for every point $x$, and for each $x$ there is an integer $n_x$ such that $\pi_i(X,x)=0$ for $i>n_x$.
additional_logical_suppliers.disposition: Supplies the exact meaning of local finiteness and the alternating higher-homotopy weights referenced in the scope remark.

additional_logical_suppliers.exact_interface_excerpt:
Thus the first factor is the subrepresentation and the second is the
quotient. This normalization has no Euler-form sign twist, no division by
automorphism orders, and no additional Tate twist. Each dimension vector has
only finitely many decompositions into \(\mathbf a+\mathbf b\), so the product
on the direct sum is defined.

The zero dimension component is \(\mathbb Q\); its element \(1\) is the unit
once the unit calculation in
